title: Customer escalation: rapid hotpatch for long-tail 5xx waves with connection throttle and safe-response swimlane
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Summary:
High-severity customer escalations reporting intermittent 5xx and streaming timeouts when tenants issue large concurrent streaming generation requests with retries enabled. Impacted tenants observe a wavey pattern: short period of elevated 502/504, followed by retries that amplify connection pressure and KV-cache churn which in turn triggers further long-tail 5xx.

Observed scope and signals:
- Affects ~4 large customers (enterprise tier) and several medium tenants during peak bursts; approximate affected request fraction ~0.8-1.5% of total hosted traffic during incident windows.
- Traces show tail latency and an increase in inflight connection count on frontdoor proxies and inference gateway pods. KV-cache eviction rates spike concurrently with sustained streaming workload.
- Correlating metrics: kv_cache_evictions_per_min, proxy_connection_wait_pct, streaming_partial_response_rate, tenant_retry_amplification_index.
- Support tickets: ZD#55421, ZD#55425.

Root-cause hypothesis (working):
A combination of factors: (1) streaming sessions with long-lived connections hold local resources in proxy + runtime; (2) client SDKs retry aggressively on partial timeouts; (3) KV cache compaction/reshard events leave the runtime temporarily slower at serving some sequences; (4) request/retry waves produce head-of-line pressure in connection pools leading to 5xx responses from overloaded runtime workers.

Immediate mitigations applied (hotpatch):
1) Tenant soft-connection-throttle: deployed an admission-layer throttle per-tenant that caps new long-lived streaming connections and returns graceful 429/524 guidance for callers that exceed safe concurrency (opaque to normal short requests).
2) Transparent fallback swimlane: for tenants on affected model families we added a runtime-path that will route new requests to a pre-quantized CPU-compatible variant when the GPU pool latency crosses SLO thresholds. This preserves partial response semantics without returning hard 5xx for most requests.
3) Guarded retry-coordination: updated API edge to honor an adaptive-retry header and impose exponential jitter backoff for client retries during detected incident windows.

Proposed permanent fixes and roadmap items:
- Short-term (next 2 sprints): implement connection admission controller with hysteresis and per-tenant concurrency budgets; add KV cache eviction smoothing (batch compaction windows) and ensure compaction does not co-occur with heavy inflight streaming workloads.
- Mid-term: kernel scheduling improvements to prioritize streaming tails, and smarter KV sync that avoids eviction storms during reshards.
- Long-term: service-level tenant pacing and predictive prefetching of KV prefixes for hot tenants, plus SDK-level safe-retry defaults and clearer client guidance.

Rollout/rollback plan for hotpatch + permanent change:
- Canary: deploy admission controller to one region (us-west-2) and to 5% of runtime-serving clusters for 24 hours; monitor 502/504 rate, avg/95/99 latency, and connection_wait_pct.
- Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 72 hours if no regression.
- Rollback: revert admission controller and fallback routing if error rate increases by >20% or any P0 customer reports regression.

Customer comms and support actions:
- Draft notice prepared for affected customers explaining mitigations and recommended SDK config (reduced retry aggressiveness and connection keepalive tuning). Link: https://confluence.redwood.company/incident/ENG-246813-customer-notice
- Assigned SE liaison for top 4 customers to provide tailored rollout and validation.

Acceptance/QA checklist for release:
- Unit + integration tests for admission controller paths and fallback routing.
- Chaos replay: synthetic surge replay to validate hysteresis and fallback correctness.
- E2E test: streaming acceptance tests with backpressure scenarios.
- Telemetry: new dashboards and alerts for kv_cache_evictions, tenant_connection_pressure, fallback_rate, and retry_amplification_index.

Postmortem deliverables:
- Root-cause writeup, timeline, and action items (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- SDK guidance update and sample code for safe retry settings (owner: DevRel).
- Permanent mitigation delivery plan tied to runtime-1.20 milestone.
